title: "Week 4 demo: sorption and parent transformation"

When parent concentration falls in water, how much has moved onto solids and how much has transformed?

Use with [organic contaminants](../organic-contaminants/notes.qmd) and [activity C](../organic-contaminants/exercise.qmd#activity-c-a-fate-model-in-r). This working week groups soils, waste chemistry, and contaminant fate.

## Predict first

Predict which control changes the phase split and which changes the total-parent half-life. Keep the outer system boundary around both water and solid.

## Questions to try

1. Choose **U at day 20**. Sum parent in water and parent on solid, then add the transformed-parent accounting term. Compare with the initial 1.00 mg.
2. Move only Kd. Observe the two parent phase amounts and check whether total parent changes at the selected time.
3. Choose **U at day 30**, then **V at day 30**. Explain the difference in both phase preference and half-life.
4. Choose **No sorption at time zero**. Verify the limiting case. Then move time to one half-life and check the remaining parent fraction.

## Hand check and static reference

| Reference case | Total parent remaining | Water parent concentration |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| U: Kd 100 L/kg, half-life 10 days, day 20 | 0.250 mg | 0.125 mg/L |
| U at day 30 | 0.125 mg | 0.0625 mg/L |
| V: Kd 10 L/kg, half-life 30 days, day 30 | 0.500 mg | 0.4545 mg/L |

The initial parent is 1.00 mg in 1.00 L water plus 0.0100 kg dry solid.
For U, the phase split is one half in each phase. Two half-lives leave one
quarter of the total parent, giving 0.125 mg in water and 0.125 mg on solid.

## Model conditions

These are fictitious neutral compounds under rapid equilibrium with constant Kd. Parent transformation has the **same** first-order coefficient in both phases, so the total parent follows `M = M₀ exp(−kt)` with `k = ln(2)/half-life`. At each time, `Cwater = M/(Vwater + Kd × msolid)`. There is no inflow, export, gas transfer, or new input. The transformed-parent curve records mass of initial parent that has changed identity; it is not measured product mass, proof of mineralisation, or a toxicity result. Phase-specific transformation or slow desorption requires another kinetic model.

## Explain the result

Under what change of model assumptions could stronger sorption affect the apparent parent persistence, rather than only the phase split?
